rule: Each decision authorizes a production change only for a finding REPRODUCED on the audited base (regressions_base_340c566.json / families_base_340c566.json). Owners are repaired at the seam the finding names; accepted milestone foundations stay as they are (M02 timeout-is-not-cancellation, M07 cleanup rules, M08 insertion broker, M11 transform gates, M12 typed note outcomes, M13 one-logical-job usage, M14 approval/undo service and all-version exposure).

decisions.decision: Current-version family integrity. At the current schema version a missing table is external damage (each migration commits its DDL and version stamp in one transaction); a store that holds tables but no version stamp lost its schema_meta and is checked the same way, before any migration runs, against the schema its tables show (the newest migration that created any table present; a table only a later migration creates was never there and is created by the upgrade), after a pre-repair backup whatever else it lost. The repair path refuses to open — a recoverable corruption report, the pre-repair backup untouched — when any surviving row of the table's family shows the lost table carried authority or user-authored content. It recreates a table empty only when that table is derivable or record-only (daily_aggregates is rebuilt from usage_facts by the launch drift check; job_deletions is backfilled by the v11 statements; purge_intents keeps its M02 policy; m14_operation_receipts and usage_meta are session-scoped/derivable; sampling_decisions, example_tags, export_manifests, profile_snapshots and job_targets carry records, not authority — each named in schema_family_subledger.json), or when its whole family is gone. The vocabulary family is M05's (M05-AUDIT-18): the Store repairs it and VocabularyStore.integrity_report governs what the app does. A genuinely older store (schema < current) upgrades exactly as before; a fresh store opens empty.

Recovery Copy Last Raw goes through the existing guarded-copy authority (AppDelegate._guarded_copy). While an insertion owns the clipboard the copy is refused: the Recovery menu item reads that it was not copied because the clipboard is busy with a pending paste, and the content-free event dictation.raw_copy_refused (reason clipboard_payload_pending) is emitted; a later successful copy, or a later failure, restores the item. No second clipboard authority and no change to the M08 broker.

TransformStore.update_transform reads the authoritative row, merges the named fields, validates (legacy, built-in mode, shortcut), updates the whole editable definition and serializes the same object as the preserved revision inside ONE writer op. The Transforms editor follows the M10 editor discipline: it binds the rendered transform id, revision and the form as shown (the built-in placeholder included); Update sends only the fields the user changed, which the store merges into the row as it is now — an untouched field, auto-apply included, is never sent back; a refresh refills an unedited editor, rebinds one whose row already holds what is typed, and marks an edited one as changed elsewhere. After a successful Update the editor refills from the definition the store returned, so it shows the row as stored.

The Transforms editor fills every control of the selected row: the instruction text view is made read-only through setEditable_ (an NSTextView has no setEnabled_), so selection never aborts before the instruction is shown.

The collector records whether a normalization whose evidence failed to retain had CHANGED the text (content-free normalization_retention {failed_step, input_changed}). cleanup_qualification_in treats missing_reasons.normalization == retention_write_failed with no normalization reference as exact raw input only when the producer recorded input_changed false; otherwise the example is not cleanup-eligible (reason normalization_input_not_retained). Healthy unchanged normalization (a retained ledger) keeps the raw input and its tier.

History resolves one job's CURRENT attempt: the training manifest is authoritative only when its attempt equals the job row's attempt; otherwise the current attempt's attempt-tagged History artifacts are used; when neither exists — the current attempt left no stage of its own — the stages are absent with reason current_attempt_unavailable. An earlier attempt's evidence is never shown as the current job's text, and its example's state does not govern Teach on the current attempt's own text. Attempt-1 evidence itself is kept.

Your Voice counts one speech contribution per logical job: the job's highest attempt among all its examples, whatever their state (ties: the latest published), is the job's contribution; when that example is not live or lacks its own retained raw transcript, the job contributes nothing. Its other attempts are counted as excluded superseded_attempt and stay inspectable as training evidence. Snippet, background-speech, user-exclusion and repeated-text filters apply after, and an excluded contribution never falls back to an older attempt. The exact-input fence covers that blocking latest attempt too: a change of its state during the computation restarts it. The 10-dictation / 2,000-word floor counts logical jobs.

The Transforms Add form preallocates one transform id per logical Add and keeps it until the outcome is known; TransformStore.add_transform with a caller-chosen id is idempotent (the identical definition already committed returns it; a different definition under that id refuses id_in_use). An admitted timeout on Add, Update or Enable/Disable renders 'outcome unknown' (never 'not saved'/'not toggled'); a pre-admission refusal still says not saved. Store timeout semantics are unchanged.

Save to Scratchpad keeps one pending note id per displayed transform result; an admitted timeout keeps it, and the preview panel returns with the result and an outcome-unknown title; the next Save of the same result reads the note back and creates it only when absent. A save refused or failed before it could commit, or made while the Scratchpad is unavailable, returns the panel as not saved and keeps no pending id. M12's typed note outcomes are unchanged.

History Copy/Move into the Scratchpad keeps one pending transfer per rendered row (its destination note id, and for Move the deletion phase). An unknown create returns create_unknown and a repeat reconciles the same note id; after a durable destination note an admitted source-deletion timeout returns source_deletion_unknown with the note id; a repeat reuses the destination note and settles only the deletion (moved when the source is already gone). The original M09 Move/Teach repairs are not reopened.

A speech-derived technical term is named by the canonical recorded in the job's frozen applied-rules artifact (qualified: the job's own vocabulary_applied_rules artifact, digest checked), grouped by (entry id, applied canonical). A rule applied in speech without a qualifiable frozen record is not named — those dictations are counted in technical_terms_unrecorded ('applied spelling not recorded') — and never labeled with the current dictionary spelling. The current dictionary still decides which rules count (approved and enabled now); dictionary usage counters stay a separately labeled current view.

Export Validate acknowledges at once ('validating …'), runs the standalone validator on the Hub's background worker (_in_background, key validate), and publishes its result into export-pane state bound to the validated destination and its action token. The pane renderer keeps the latest validation for the destination on screen; a training refresh never repaints over it; only a newer Validate or Export, or a different destination, supersedes it — an Export retires the token of any Validate still running when it is pressed, and while an Export into a folder runs — or its outcome is unknown, until an Export of that folder settles — Validate of that folder is refused with that reason (it would describe a package in mid-replacement); the folder is the one Export resolves (~ expanded, a trailing slash the same folder), and a Validate of another folder runs as usual. A second Export into a folder is refused while one into it runs. Every validator check is unchanged.

Publication intent. Before the publication op the exporter commits export_manifests state 'publishing' (destination, fingerprint and manifest recorded); the publication op re-checks dependencies, marks it complete and renames. Every build first reconciles its destination, whatever export id it carries: each 'publishing' intent recorded for that destination with no publication of it in flight in this process is settled conservatively — the export's own package at the destination (its manifest names the export id and the offline validator passes) is recorded 'published_unconfirmed', never 'complete', no new consent or exposure granted, and left in place; with no such package the intent is recorded 'failed' (publication_not_performed). Only moved-aside earlier exports this exporter names and owns are touched: an export-id suffix, no build of it in flight in this process (a build is in flight from the moment its staging exists), and a folder a build may replace. Such an earlier export is put back when the destination is free; otherwise it is removed only when this build completes, as a completed build removes the export it replaced. Every build records a building intent when its staging exists, and its staging carries an owner file naming the build, held under an exclusive lock by the building process until the publication op renames it (the lock ends with that process, however it ends); its destination is recorded absolute. At launch and before every build, each building intent whose build is not in flight in this process and whose owner file no build holds has its staging removed (any earlier export it moved aside put back) and is recorded failed (build_interrupted), so an export LocalFlow quit or crashed during leaves no copy of recordings behind (Evaluation E19); a build still running in another process is never touched, and an intent whose folder is not reachable now (a drive not mounted) is left for a later launch. A repeated export id while that export is still being built here is refused without touching its record. Nothing else beside the destination is touched. A retry of the same export id that finds its package published_unconfirmed is refused with that explanation.

The Review tab offers Undo approval for the selected approved learned rule: the existing LearningService.undo_approval with the rendered candidate id, an operation id kept across an unknown outcome, the existing typed refusal (user_modified_since_approval) shown as text, and a review refresh after. No other Hub change.

STATUS.json gains an explicit current_state projection — store_schema_version (derived from the code), production_commit and evidence (the current remediation's production commit and evidence records), performance (where current performance is interpreted) and may_run_next — and keeps the M14 implementation fields verbatim under historical_implementation. Historical records are never rewritten.

VERIFICATION.html's M07 section carries stable checks for the still-open M07 obligations (the long-prompt cleanup trial, the adjudicated real-text stratum), PENDING and owned; no human pass is recorded or implied.

policies.decision: Writer contention is measured after correctness (current dictation writer wait beside profile, export and mining work, pairwise) and reported with its workload identity; no deletion/requalification/exposure check is removed for speed. The historical ~205 ms / ~174 ms maxima remain observations under their recorded fixtures.
No AI-powered Your Voice interpretation in this remediation: no provider, key, network dependency or local model interpretation. Recorded as a later optional product phase.

History Paste Again while the Hub is in front needs an explicit user-facing destination policy; this campaign changes nothing there and carries it as an open product decision with native qualification, not as an insertion bug.

Direct SQL rewriting of the store is outside the supported threat model. Supported producers bind task/source identity, export requalifies every pair, corrupt data fails closed; the pair-forgery residual stays a defense-in-depth note unless a supported bypass is found.

policy_refinements.supersedes_current_rule: Application/window click authority for History Paste Again; historical POLICY-D03 decisions and evidence remain unchanged.
policy_refinements.trigger: Packaged native PA-7 titlebar click produced a confirmed 58-character AX replacement into the previously focused field.
policy_refinements.decision: Only a fresh actual click resolving to a currently valid editable AX text destination grants History Paste Again authority. Prove hit containment, editability/writability, enabled state, owning process/window; bind exact element/window and revalidate before reconciliation and insertion. Non-editable or unsupported hits grant no authority and keep the picker armed under its existing timeout. Never fall back to focused/default/stale fields. Normal PTT, Recovery Paste Last Result Again, M08 strict replacement, source binding, clipboard policy and model behavior are unchanged.
